title: Notes must agree at the joins.
body: You revise the wrong version, lose marks, and stop trusting your own notes.

title: Give each note its own card.
body: A wrong link survives review, and every answer built on it inherits the error.

title: Keep the red join red.
body: The client finds the problem before you do, and trust in every report drops.

title: Map the joins, then merge.
body: Broken imports and dead links ship, and a weekend goes to tracing them by hand.

title: Show both sides of the edge.
body: You act on the wrong answer and never learn that a second answer existed.

title: One owner for every join.
body: The shipped version contradicts the plan, and nobody can say which copy was meant.

title: Seven opinions, one line.
body: The meeting stalls, someone picks a number by rank, and the rest stop reporting honestly.

title: Keep both. Mark the join.
body: The assistant answers confidently from the newest note, and the client's real words are lost.

title: Test the gate by breaking it.
body: A checker that cannot fail gives false comfort, and the gaps reach readers.

title: Trust the parts that agree.
body: You repeat a made-up detail to a client because it sounded as sure as the rest.

title: Fold only the joins that agree.
body: A disagreement between agents is erased without a trace, so the team ships an answer that another agent had already contradicted.

title: Odd joins wait for a person.
body: A strange result reaches a leader's report with no person ever having looked at it, and decisions get made on it.

title: Every push meets the gate.
body: One badly shaped file breaks the shared viewer for every reader, and nobody knows which push did it.

title: Let every join pull back.
body: Every small change sends the model wandering, so hours go into hand-fixing shapes that should hold on their own.

title: Floppy parts have fewer joins.
body: Guessing which part is firm wastes experiments and leads to building on the floppy end.

title: See every link below the top.
body: Money and attention go to what is visible, while the small project everything stands on fails unnoticed.

title: Credit should flow down the links.
body: The small projects everything depends on burn out unpaid, and one day the big ones fall with them.

title: Draw only links you can show.
body: Readers trust links nobody built, so reviews, plans and agents act on wiring that does not exist.

title: Let the unfinished joins glow.
body: Teams plan on top of work that does not exist yet, and the surprise lands late and expensive.

title: Rules on top, parts below.
body: New people and new agents can't find their way, so they guess, and the guesses become bugs.

title: A wiki with pins.
body: New people and AI helpers read the wiki as true. One broken link sends both to a dead page, and the wrong answer travels.

title: Merge, and keep the seams.
body: Two teams' knowledge becomes one source nobody believes. People go back to asking each other, and the merge was wasted.

title: The same mistake, pinned.
body: The team pays for the same mistake again and again, and readers stop believing fixes stick.

title: Don't touch the gate.
body: Green checks that were bent, not earned. The team ships the gap and trusts the dashboard.

title: We choose the pins.
body: One overclaim and a careful audience stops trusting the parts that are real.

title: Try first. Then the gate opens.
body: Hours of reading with nothing kept. The next puzzle starts from zero.

title: Find the pin first.
body: Every problem costs full price. Nothing learned on one carries to the next.

title: Small changes, one counter.
body: A quarter of fine edits leaves docs nobody recognises. People who learned the old version get it wrong.

title: AI writes. The gate checks.
body: Either you read everything and lose the week, or you trust it blind and ship its mistakes to customers.

title: Two copies, one seam.
body: The doc lies to everyone who builds from it, and the next agent or hire builds the wrong thing.

title: Give every note a label.
body: A decision gets reversed in front of the client, and the team stops trusting the summary.

title: Hand over only the right cards.
body: The one rule that mattered is broken in public, and the fix is to read everything yourself next time.

title: One fact at every joint.
body: Two halves of the work are built for different dates, and nobody notices until they are joined.

title: Private cards stay home.
body: A client's private detail lands in someone else's work, and trust is gone for good.

title: Send the wiring, not the pile.
body: Answers about how parts connect are guessed, and changes made on those answers break things.

title: Draw the sockets first.
body: Results cannot be reproduced, so every rerun costs a full rebuild and a week of doubt.

title: See every joint first.
body: Every release becomes a gamble, and teams stop changing anything at all.

title: Add the missing piece.
body: Hours lost forcing joins, and a chain that breaks the moment one tool changes its output.

title: Each helper gets its own part.
body: Work is done three times and undone twice, and the bill for helpers grows while nothing ships.

title: Find the joint that slipped.
body: Every wrong answer means rereading the whole run, and fixes land in the wrong place.

title: Build it once, with slots.
body: Hours of prompt writing redone per client, and each rewrite forgets something the last one had.

title: Stop when the counter hits zero.
body: Endless rewriting by feel: time burned, and the author misses the flaws only a fresh reader would see.

title: Send only what clears the gate.
body: Wrong answers shipped on gut feel, then found by a customer or a reviewer.

title: One line for every puzzle.
body: Results change run to run, so nothing can be compared or trusted.

title: Every try gets a tick.
body: The good version is lost; hours redone; nobody can say what changed.

title: A small gate picks the road.
body: Money and minutes burned on easy questions; hard questions rushed.

title: Check every join in the chain.
body: One small early slip spreads into a useless final result, and you only find it at the end.

title: Keep the judge pinned.
body: A loop that can move its own yardstick reports progress while quality falls, and nobody can tell from the numbers.

title: One change, then measure.
body: Gains can't be explained or repeated, and a harmful change hides inside a helpful bundle.

title: Let it draft the cards first.
body: Vague one-line asks get vague answers, so people give up on the tool or trust a guess.

title: Hunches don't fit the slot.
body: Releases ship on somebody's say-so, and afterwards nobody can tell what the ship decision actually rested on.

title: When unsure, the gate stays shut.
body: Every "don't know" quietly becomes a yes. Wrong orders go out, and the incident report reads "the system was not sure".

title: Every step gets a tick.
body: Double payments, double emails, double merges. Each one costs money and trust, and has to be clawed back by hand.

title: Doing waits behind the gate.
body: A wrong price or the wrong client goes out in your name. Nothing reads it first, and nothing can call it back.

title: Five small gates, not one.
body: Real emails are flagged and real scams pass. The score looks like a model problem when it is really a question problem.

title: First, check the ruler.
body: Decisions get made on a number that moved because the ruler broke, not because the work changed.

title: Coin flips go to a person.
body: Money leaves on a coin toss, and no one can undo it. The customer loses trust and the money doesn't come back.

title: Leave the flag where it is.
body: Every smoothed-over mismatch becomes a trap for the next person. Hours are lost rediscovering what someone already saw.

title: Every claim faces the same gates.
body: Weeks spent reading hype, and a team picks a tool because of a title.

title: Readers pass a one-way gate.
body: Curious people break live systems, so teams stop sharing, and the people who need to understand the system never see it.

title: Every miss gets a new gate.
body: A customer finds the bug first, so trust is lost and the fix costs more than the check would have.

title: Add a different gate.
body: Each extra copy of the same check costs time and money and catches nothing new, while customers keep hitting the same kind of bug.

title: Turn every miss into a gate.
body: Every miss gets fixed by hand, one at a time, and the same kind of mistake returns next week.

title: The old bug hits a gate.
body: Fixed bugs come back, and each one is paid for twice: once to fix it and once to find it again.

title: Fresh eyes try to break it.
body: Self-review ships the mistakes the maker can't see, and a reader or reviewer finds them in public.

title: Check the pin before the work.
body: A perfectly checked program can still do the wrong thing, and the green result makes everyone stop looking.

title: Find the first broken joint.
body: Every failed agent run costs an hour of reading logs, and the real cause is often far from where it showed up.

title: Show one real example.
body: Time goes into chasing fixes that were only ever promised, and confident claims are believed without anything to try.

title: Seven gates watch every frame.
body: Small flaws you can't see on your own screen reach every viewer, and they read as carelessness.

title: Check the work, not its label.
body: Decisions get made on green reports while customers see the broken thing, and trust in every report drops.

title: Every answer keeps its receipt.
body: A wrong answer gets acted on, and nobody can trace it, fix it at the source, or warn anyone else.

title: Give every note a label.
body: A guess hardens into a citation, then into a decision, and nobody can tell which line was ever read.

title: Every step leaves a mark.
body: Every failure becomes a guessing game. The fix takes hours, and the same bad step runs again tonight.

title: Draw only the joins you see.
body: Leaders fund, promise and staff against a picture of a system that does not exist yet.

title: Test where the parts join.
body: Green tests ship a page that freezes for real users, and the bug hides between owners.

title: A gate after every step.
body: The bad answer ships, and debugging starts at the wrong end of the line.

title: Let the check only look.
body: A report nobody can repeat. Leaders act on numbers that describe a workspace that no longer exists.

title: Some numbers get a pin.
body: Each AI redesign drifts a safety or comfort number, and someone has to catch it by hand, every time.

title: Start with the small card.
body: More context costs more and answers worse, and the one fact that mattered never gets read.

title: Three runs, one gate.
body: A slip in one tool becomes a published result, and nobody can tell it apart from a correct one.

title: Let the colours ring.
body: A page ships with colours that fight, and the client sees it before you do.

title: Keep the reading pair pinned.
body: Leaders present to a room that can't read the screen, and the message is lost.

title: Three parts, many songs.
body: Weeks go into sound that cannot be rebuilt, reused or checked.

title: Finished is when every gate opens.
body: Clients find the problems first, and every fix after delivery costs trust.

title: Shrink it through the gates.
body: The brand vanishes exactly where people see it most: tabs, phones, feeds.

title: Draw the order as one line.
body: Nights of runs wasted, and wrong answers built on half-finished steps.

title: Pull every thread into view.
body: You repeat old work, and miss the idea that ties a talk together.

title: Every shape gets one pin.
body: Learners decode your shapes instead of your ideas, and they learn the wrong thing.

title: Taste, one tick at a time.
body: Hours of describing, and still nothing that looks like your own work.

title: Every sound on the tick.
body: Hours of nudging, redone after every edit, and the film still feels off.

title: Every frame lives on the line.
body: A frame you cannot pause on is a frame you cannot teach from; screenshots, reviews and replays all disagree.

title: Every join must hold.
body: A long cut that does not hang together costs a class session and the learners' trust in every film after it.

title: Two copies, one card.
body: Learners read the screen, reviewers read the script, and neither knows the other is wrong.

title: Run the ring end to end.
body: The problem ships exactly where nobody looked: the middle of the lesson.

title: Nothing fake gets past the door.
body: A build breaks at best. At worst, someone registers that fake name with bad code inside.

title: Turn each rule into a door.
body: Teams lose trust in the AI and in their own rules, and review turns into rereading everything.

title: The old bug meets a door.
body: Every repeat costs the fix twice and tells users the team is not listening.

title: Lay the cards side by side.
body: Any choice built on that score cannot tell the good assistant from the bad one.

title: Every version gets a tick.
body: You cannot stand behind work you cannot trace, and a silent change becomes your mistake in front of a client.

title: Put a ring on every turn.
body: Viewers drop off, and some cannot watch at all, so the lesson never lands.
